punchline: Rome turned defeated enemies and freed slaves into citizens, and kept growing.
thirty_sec: Mary Beard says Rome did something many Greek cities did not: it gave citizenship to the people it conquered and to freed slaves. Under Claudius, a speech argued that Gallic notables should sit in the senate, and a bronze copy of it survives in Lyon. In AD 212 Caracalla gave citizenship to almost every free person in the empire. Rome grew by turning outsiders into members.
